content: The task of interpreting and following natural language (NL) navigation instructions involves interleaving different signals, at the very least the linguistic utterance and the representation of the world. For example, in turn right on the first intersection, the instruction needs to be interpreted, and a specific object in the world (the intersection) needs to be located in order to execute the instruction. In NL navigation studies, the representation of the world may be provided via visual sensors BIBREF0, BIBREF1, BIBREF2, BIBREF3, BIBREF4 or as a symbolic world representation. This work focuses on navigation based on a symbolic world representation (referred to as a map).
